rationale: B wins because it protects the founder from math that will get killed in the first call. A writes “implying $40M or more flowed to Substack from top creators alone,” while B asks “whether $400M is gross subscription revenue before the 10% cut or net to creators” before building the business story. B also adds a sharper downside angle, “writers who never wanted to be on camera,” without pretending the answer is already known.
gaps_in_A: “$400 million in creator earnings is an inconvenient number for the subscription fatigue narrative” invents an outside discourse from the supplied facts; the proof list admits it still needs documentation.

“YouTube runs on ads. Substack's video play bets that creators would rather own their audience.” drags in YouTube/TikTok economics not supplied in the update. It may be true, but it is not grounded here.

“implying $40M or more flowed to Substack from top creators alone” treats the $400M creator figure as clean revenue math before proving whether the number is gross, net, or bounded to subscription revenue.
“the broader debate over creator monetization models is active” is a fake why-now unless backed with current coverage receipts.
gaps_in_B: “Next step: meanest-editor” is the wrong handoff for an angle set; after choosing the defensible angle, this should go to journalist-fit-check or reporter matching.
“Reporters will write this whether or not Substack pitches it” overstates certainty. Make it a risk to prepare for, not prophecy.
“one number they will share” assumes a creator will disclose economics. The proof list catches the gap, but the angle should not sound like that source already exists.
